statuses.guaranteed: Deterministic and blocking. Implemented, and a behavioural test proves it.
statuses.advisory: Projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours it is not observable from outside. Documentation, not enforcement.
statuses.planned: Specified and not implemented. Named so the omission is visible.
statuses.rejected: Considered and deliberately refused, with the reason recorded.

edge_kinds.specified_by: the document that defines the claim
edge_kinds.proved_by: the behavioural test that proves it

nodes.label: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key
nodes.note: A restricted YAML subset. Tabs, anchors, flow maps and multi-line scalars are refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.label: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist
Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
nodes.note: The path must exist, be executable, and be invoked by the named dispatcher. A hook that invokes it and discards the exit code counts as not wired.

nodes.label: Exit codes are a contract, and no code means "warn and continue"
Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
nodes.note: Running update twice leaves the byte-identical file. The test asserts the hash.

nodes.label: Every generated instruction file is fingerprinted, and a hand edit is detected
A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
nodes.note: How a repository that already has a hand-written CLAUDE.md adopts Majordomus. An edit outside the markers is never drift; an edit inside them is caught. Malformed markers are refused, not guessed at.

nodes.label: Wiring is found in a hook or in any subhook of the directory that hook dispatches to
nodes.note: The finding names the file that actually carries the invocation. A subhook that is not executable is reported as not wired, because the dispatcher skips it.

nodes.label: Every rule the tool enforces is declared in one registry, and doctor proves each one is reached by the command that claims to run it
nodes.note: A doctrine whose validator does not exist, a validator no doctrine declares, a command that never dispatches, a blocking rule whose command cannot exit non-zero, a missing test, and CI that swallows the suite are six separate failures with six separate messages. Each is mutation-tested.

nodes.label: A doctrine's class is what decides whether a violation stops the command, not a label beside it
nodes.note: The test changes checkpoint freshness from advisory to blocking in a copy of the registry and asserts that check's exit code moves from 0 to 10. There are two classes and no override.

nodes.label: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event, and a malformed line is a failure rather than a skipped record
nodes.note: The reader skips a bad line rather than crashing, and check, doctor and watch all report it. The ledger is the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct.

nodes.label: A decision record without a task, a head and a reason is reported, and does not block
nodes.note: decisions.md is hand-editable by design, so an unattributable entry is a warning. finish still refuses when a profile requires a record it cannot find.

nodes.label: An entry in the questions store that does not parse blocks acceptance exactly as an unresolved question does
nodes.note: A gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one, so an unreadable question is not a lesser problem than an open one.

nodes.label: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure
nodes.note: Covers name and filename mismatch, an empty description, an unknown front-matter key, missing front matter, and a block token used inline.

nodes.label: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
nodes.note: update refuses, offers a diff, and overwrites only under an explicit flag.

nodes.label: The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check
nodes.note: Over budget, nothing is written at all.

nodes.label: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve
A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
Installing into a repository that already has an installation is refused
Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
Nothing performs a network call, evaluates generated text, or deletes recursively
A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
nodes.note: A scope path that escapes the repository root is refused. Starting a second task while one is active is refused.

nodes.label: Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored
nodes.note: A handover body that tries to set one is rejected rather than merged.

nodes.label: check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now
A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
State read back is labelled exact, advanced, diverged or different_context against git
Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
nodes.note: Reported, never blocking. Work in progress is reported and never blocked.

nodes.label: watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift
handover writes an append-only record with computed front matter and required sections
nodes.note: A body with a missing or empty required section is refused and names the sections.

nodes.label: Handovers carry durable facts, never conversation transcripts
finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet
An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
nodes.note: no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist. failed means the work could not be done. They are different facts.

nodes.label: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
nodes.note: The axes are validated and projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours them is not observable from outside the worker.

nodes.label: A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model
nodes.note: Mapping a class to a concrete model is left to whoever runs the worker. Majordomus never selects or invokes a model.

nodes.label: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more
nodes.note: majordomus context now assembles a briefing from those toggles, and that selection is guaranteed (see context-assembly). This claim stays advisory because nothing measures what the worker actually read once it has been handed the briefing.

nodes.label: Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed
A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported
nodes.note: The staleness report is guaranteed. Whether the worker checkpoints is not.

nodes.label: The context a worker is given is assembled from durable state in authority order, and what a profile excludes is excluded
nodes.note: Git first, then task and profile, then blockers, then authored records, then history. The profile's context block decides what is offered; it is the only code that reads those fields.

nodes.label: The assembled context obeys a line budget, and every section it drops is named with its reason
nodes.note: The count is of the printed document, not of its sections. Git, task, profile and open blockers are never dropped; record bodies degrade to a pointer before they disappear.

nodes.label: A checkpoint is a capped progress record with computed identity, and a body over the cap is refused rather than truncated
nodes.note: The cap is what keeps a checkpoint distinct from a handover. Mode 0600, created atomically, never staged.

nodes.label: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
nodes.note: Same worktree and branch, else same branch, else nothing. Ties within one second are broken by ledger order. Absence is reported as absence.

nodes.label: The ledger is readable back as operational history, filtered by task, event and time
nodes.note: What happened, when, for which task, at which head, and what outcome was accepted. Never what anyone said.

nodes.label: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
nodes.note: Refuses to overwrite an existing archive, and does nothing when the ledger is under its cap.

nodes.label: A decision is recorded with its reason and its task, and is superseded by a later entry rather than edited
nodes.note: --why is required. --supersedes refuses text matching no recorded decision. Task and head are computed.

nodes.label: An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an entry the gate cannot parse is a failure rather than a silent pass
nodes.note: A gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one, so check, doctor and watch all fail on a malformed entry.

nodes.label: A repository-local prompt renders against a closed set of state tokens, and an unknown token is an error
nodes.note: No conditionals, loops, includes or shell. A prompt that silently renders a misspelled token as literal text is worse than one that refuses.

nodes.label: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
nodes.note: A fixed-string grep in authority order. No ranking, no embedding, no index that could fall out of step with the records it describes.

nodes.label: Every continuity store is proven reachable through its own command, not merely present on disk
nodes.note: doctor runs the resolver, renders every prompt asset, validates both parsed stores and builds the context. A directory of records that no command reads is the failure this tool exists to catch.

nodes.label: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented
nodes.note: The corpus is a handful of Markdown files and one JSONL. An index or an embedding store would be a second source of truth that has to be kept in step with the first, and a scan is faster than that problem. Revisited only if a repository appears where the scan is measurably too slow.

nodes.label: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope
nodes.note: The record is tracked, so it travels with the branch. check, finish --check and watch report a foreign record and enforce nothing from it; finish refuses to write to it. A record from before the field existed is treated as local, so upgrading does not turn an installation red.

nodes.label: A blocking question will keep blocking after the work is handed to a new task
nodes.note: Today a question is attached to the task that opened it, so handing over and starting a new task leaves it unresolved and no longer blocking. Found by running the documented end-to-end sequence rather than by review. Needs a decision about whether questions transfer with a handover or the gate widens; both are wrong in some case, so it is published as unfixed rather than guessed at.

nodes.label: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
nodes.note: v0.2. The one implementation studied was rolled back within days because its limits were global constants rather than task-derived.

nodes.label: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
nodes.note: v0.3. Nothing in v0.1 measures token spend. Any estimated_ field is labelled and excluded from enforcement.

nodes.label: Cost per accepted outcome will be reported from measured data only
Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
nodes.note: v0.5. Recommendations only. Majordomus does not invoke a model.

nodes.label: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers
Dependencies between tasks are deliberately not represented
nodes.note: No use case in the evidence justified a dependency graph. Listed so that the omission is visible rather than assumed to be an oversight. Revisited only when a real case appears.
